newsitem.title: USA: Utilities sue TVA for selling power outside fence.
newsitem.headline: Utilities sue TVA for selling power outside fence.

text.p: Five utilities Thursday filed a lawsuit against Tennessee Valley Authority, alleging that it was selling power outside its designated area, violating its Congressional mandate.
The lawsuit, filed by three Southern Company utilities, Duke Power Co, and an Entergy Corp utility, also asked the U.S. District Court in Birmingham, Alabama to block the allegedly illegal sales.
A spokesman for Southern Co said TVA was using customers within its territory as conduits to sell power to Commonwealth Edison, a subsidiary of Unicom Corp, and others outside its territory.

TVA was selling power in paper transactions to its legal customers, including Cinergy Corp and Louisville Gas and Electric, who then arranged to sell power outside TVA's fence, and asked TVA to deliver it, Southern Co said.
TVA said it had not seen the lawsuit yet. "We will comment appropriately through the courts," a TVA spokesman said.
The utilities have been battling TVA on all fronts as the electricity market becomes more open, arguing that it is unfair for them to compete against a federally-backed power producer.

Last year, a federal judge ruled in favor of three Southern Company utilities against TVA, saying that TVA could not sell power to a marketing affiliate of Louisville Gas and Electric, even though the utility was one of its customers.
